parameters.content:
## 00 — TRIGGER

TEMPLATE_WF14_RECONCILIATION_ANALYTICS_V2 · v2.0.0
Contratos: ANALYTICS_EVENT v2.2 · TEMPLATE_DATA v2.2
Rollback: WF14 v1 — desactivar este workflow; v1 vuelve a sincronizar (§12)

Cada 5 minutos. **El dashboard no espera a este workflow**: si WF14 no corre en
una hora, los KPIs del panel siguen siendo correctos porque salen de
`wf_call_jobs` y `wf_events`. Lo que se acumula es el trabajo de
reconciliación, que es exactamente lo que debe acumularse.

## 01 — LOAD CONFIG

Los umbrales de reconciliación son
**configuración** (`wf_settings`), no literales: cuántos minutos hace falta que
un `DISPATCHING` lleve parado para considerarlo perdido depende de la latencia
real de cada proveedor.

Si `/api/settings` no responde, se usan los defaults documentados (los mismos
que siembra la migración) y se deja constancia en el log.

## 02 — RECONCILE CALL JOBS

Reclasifica lo que quedó a medias.
**Nunca re-despacha.**

| estado viejo | qué pasó | qué se hace |
|---|---|---|
| `CLAIMED` sin despachar | no salió llamada | → `RELEASED` (se re-reclama tras el backoff) |
| `DISPATCHING` parado | **pudo** salir | → `NEEDS_RECONCILIATION` |
| `UNKNOWN` | pudo salir | → `NEEDS_RECONCILIATION` |
| `DISPATCHED` sin post-call | salió, no llegó el resultado | → `NEEDS_RECONCILIATION` |

La diferencia entre `UNKNOWN` y `NEEDS_RECONCILIATION` importa: `UNKNOWN` es lo
que acaba de reportar el adapter; `NEEDS_RECONCILIATION` es lo que ya nadie va a
resolver solo. **Ninguno de los dos se vuelve a llamar.**

parameters.query:
UPDATE wf_call_jobs
   SET state = 'RELEASED', error_class = 'TECHNICAL', error_code = 'STALE_CLAIM',
       tech_retry_count = tech_retry_count + 1,
       next_tech_retry_at = DATE_ADD(UTC_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL
         LEAST(POW(2, tech_retry_count), 60) MINUTE),
       updated_at = UTC_TIMESTAMP()
 WHERE state = 'CLAIMED'
   AND claimed_at < DATE_SUB(UTC_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL ? MINUTE)

UPDATE wf_call_jobs
   SET state = 'NEEDS_RECONCILIATION', error_class = 'AMBIGUOUS',
       error_code = 'STALE_DISPATCHING', updated_at = UTC_TIMESTAMP()
 WHERE state = 'DISPATCHING'
   AND updated_at < DATE_SUB(UTC_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL ? MINUTE)

UPDATE wf_call_jobs
   SET state = 'NEEDS_RECONCILIATION', updated_at = UTC_TIMESTAMP()
 WHERE state = 'UNKNOWN'
   AND updated_at < DATE_SUB(UTC_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL ? MINUTE)

UPDATE wf_call_jobs
   SET state = 'NEEDS_RECONCILIATION', error_code = 'NO_POSTCALL',
       error_class = 'AMBIGUOUS', updated_at = UTC_TIMESTAMP()
 WHERE state = 'DISPATCHED'
   AND dispatched_at < DATE_SUB(UTC_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL ? MINUTE)

parameters.content:
## 03 — RECONCILE LEDGERS

Los tres ledgers de idempotencia:
conversaciones, pedidos de tool y grabaciones.

Un claim huérfano (n8n murió con la reserva tomada) **no se reintenta solo**:
pasa a revisión. Reintentar un `POST /followups`, una creación de cuenta o un
link de pago que pudo haberse ejecutado es peor que dejarlo para un humano.

parameters.query:
UPDATE wf_conversation_ledger
   SET state = 'NEEDS_RECONCILIATION', error_code = 'STALE_CLAIM'
 WHERE state = 'CLAIMED' AND followup_id IS NULL
   AND claimed_at < DATE_SUB(UTC_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL ? MINUTE)

UPDATE wf_tool_requests
   SET state = 'NEEDS_RECONCILIATION', error_code = 'STALE_CLAIM',
       updated_at = UTC_TIMESTAMP()
 WHERE state = 'CLAIMED'
   AND claimed_at < DATE_SUB(UTC_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL ? MINUTE)

UPDATE wf_recording_ledger
   SET state = 'FAILED', error_code = 'STALE_CLAIM', updated_at = UTC_TIMESTAMP()
 WHERE state = 'CLAIMED'
   AND claimed_at < DATE_SUB(UTC_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 30 MINUTE)

parameters.content:
## 04 — OPEN ISSUES

Todo lo que quedó en `NEEDS_RECONCILIATION`
se convierte en un issue con `issue_key` **determinista**: volver a detectarlo
suma `occurrences`, no crea filas nuevas. Así el panel muestra "3 llamadas a
revisar", no "3.000 alertas repetidas".

También se abre `TECH_RETRY_REPEATED` cuando un lead acumula reintentos técnicos
contra el mismo proveedor: eso no es un problema del lead, es un problema del
proveedor, y conviene verlo antes de que consuma la ventana de llamadas.

parameters.query:
INSERT INTO wf_reconciliation_issues
  (issue_key, issue_type, entity_type, entity_id, lead_id, country_iso,
   severity, state, detail_json, first_seen_at, last_seen_at)
SELECT CONCAT('CALL_NEEDS_RECONCILIATION:call_job:', j.call_job_id),
       'CALL_NEEDS_RECONCILIATION', 'call_job', j.call_job_id, j.lead_id,
       j.country_iso, 'WARN', 'OPEN',
       JSON_OBJECT('state', j.state, 'error_code', j.error_code,
                   'route_key', j.route_key, 'attempt', j.attempt,
                   'provider', j.provider),
       UTC_TIMESTAMP(), UTC_TIMESTAMP()
  FROM wf_call_jobs j
 WHERE j.state = 'NEEDS_RECONCILIATION'
   AND j.updated_at >= DATE_SUB(UTC_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 1 DAY)
ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE occurrences = occurrences + 1,
        last_seen_at = UTC_TIMESTAMP()

INSERT INTO wf_reconciliation_issues
  (issue_key, issue_type, entity_type, entity_id, lead_id, country_iso,
   severity, state, detail_json, first_seen_at, last_seen_at)
SELECT CONCAT('FOLLOWUP_NEEDS_RECONCILIATION:conversation:', l.conversation_id),
       'FOLLOWUP_NEEDS_RECONCILIATION', 'conversation', l.conversation_id,
       l.lead_id, NULL, 'ERROR', 'OPEN',
       JSON_OBJECT('state', l.state, 'error_code', l.error_code,
                   'route_key', l.route_key, 'call_job_id', l.call_job_id),
       UTC_TIMESTAMP(), UTC_TIMESTAMP()
  FROM wf_conversation_ledger l
 WHERE l.state = 'NEEDS_RECONCILIATION'
   AND l.updated_at >= DATE_SUB(UTC_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 1 DAY)
ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE occurrences = occurrences + 1,
        last_seen_at = UTC_TIMESTAMP()

INSERT INTO wf_reconciliation_issues
  (issue_key, issue_type, entity_type, entity_id, lead_id, country_iso,
   severity, state, detail_json, first_seen_at, last_seen_at)
SELECT CONCAT('TECH_RETRY_REPEATED:route:', j.route_key),
       'TECH_RETRY_REPEATED', 'route', j.route_key, NULL, j.country_iso,
       'WARN', 'OPEN',
       JSON_OBJECT('released_jobs', COUNT(*), 'provider', j.provider,
                   'max_retries', MAX(j.tech_retry_count)),
       UTC_TIMESTAMP(), UTC_TIMESTAMP()
  FROM wf_call_jobs j
 WHERE j.state = 'RELEASED'
   AND j.updated_at >= DATE_SUB(UTC_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 1 HOUR)
 GROUP BY j.route_key, j.country_iso, j.provider
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5
ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE occurrences = occurrences + 1,
        last_seen_at = UTC_TIMESTAMP(), detail_json = VALUES(detail_json)

parameters.content:
## 05 — CRM SYNC (LEGACY)

Se conserva la sincronización
`LeadStudio -> crm_leads` de v1 porque otras pantallas del panel la usan y
porque la reconciliación necesita el lado del CRM para comparar.

Usa `GET /api/leads` (reporting, sin cupo), **nunca** `/queue`: la cola es para
llamar, y consumirla acá le robaría leads a WF2.

Diferencia clave con v1: esto **ya no alimenta el dashboard del call center**.
Es una copia para comparar, no la fuente de la verdad.

## 06 — UPSERT crm_leads

`INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE` en
lotes de 500. El país sale del prefijo real del teléfono (autoritativo) y no del
campo `country` del lead, que puede venir nulo.

El `provider` de `crm_leads` **ya no** se deduce de "si aparece en
stringee_calls": en V2 la ruta y el proveedor de cada llamada están en
`wf_call_jobs`. Se conserva la columna para no romper las pantallas viejas, pero
la verdad está en el job.

parameters.query:
INSERT INTO crm_leads
  (lead_id, full_name, phone, country, country_code, language, status, stage,
   call_attempts, do_not_call, last_contacted_at, next_follow_up_at, provider,
   synced_at)
SELECT j.lead_id, j.full_name, j.phone,
       CASE WHEN j.phone LIKE '+977%' OR j.phone LIKE '977%' THEN 'nepal'
            WHEN j.phone LIKE '+52%'  OR j.phone LIKE '52%'  THEN 'mexico'
            WHEN j.phone LIKE '+91%'  OR j.phone LIKE '91%'  THEN 'india'
            WHEN j.phone LIKE '+57%'  OR j.phone LIKE '57%'  THEN 'colombia'
            WHEN j.phone LIKE '+58%'  OR j.phone LIKE '58%'  THEN 'venezuela'
            ELSE 'unknown' END,
       CASE WHEN j.phone LIKE '+977%' OR j.phone LIKE '977%' THEN '+977'
            WHEN j.phone LIKE '+52%'  OR j.phone LIKE '52%'  THEN '+52'
            WHEN j.phone LIKE '+91%'  OR j.phone LIKE '91%'  THEN '+91'
            WHEN j.phone LIKE '+57%'  OR j.phone LIKE '57%'  THEN '+57'
            WHEN j.phone LIKE '+58%'  OR j.phone LIKE '58%'  THEN '+58'
            ELSE '' END,
       j.language, j.status, j.stage, j.call_attempts, j.do_not_call,
       j.last_contacted_at, j.next_follow_up_at,
       (SELECT c.provider FROM wf_call_jobs c WHERE c.lead_id = j.lead_id
         ORDER BY c.created_at DESC LIMIT 1),
       UTC_TIMESTAMP()
  FROM JSON_TABLE(?, '$[*]' COLUMNS (
        lead_id VARCHAR(64) PATH '$.lead_id',
        full_name VARCHAR(160) PATH '$.full_name',
        phone VARCHAR(32) PATH '$.phone',
        language VARCHAR(16) PATH '$.language',
        status VARCHAR(48) PATH '$.status',
        stage VARCHAR(48) PATH '$.stage',
        call_attempts INT PATH '$.call_attempts',
        do_not_call INT PATH '$.do_not_call',
        last_contacted_at DATETIME PATH '$.last_contacted_at',
        next_follow_up_at DATETIME PATH '$.next_follow_up_at')) AS j
ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE
  full_name = VALUES(full_name), phone = VALUES(phone),
  country = VALUES(country), country_code = VALUES(country_code),
  language = VALUES(language), status = VALUES(status), stage = VALUES(stage),
  call_attempts = VALUES(call_attempts), do_not_call = VALUES(do_not_call),
  last_contacted_at = VALUES(last_contacted_at),
  next_follow_up_at = VALUES(next_follow_up_at),
  provider = COALESCE(VALUES(provider), provider),
  synced_at = VALUES(synced_at)

parameters.content:
## 07 — COMPARE LOCAL vs CRM

Dos comparaciones, ambas **solo de
lectura** sobre los datos locales:

 · **cuenta local sin reflejo en el CRM** — hay `ACCOUNT_CREATED` en
   `wf_events` y el CRM no marca la cuenta → `CRM_ACCOUNT_MISSING`
 · **estado divergente** — el lead quedó `ATTEMPTING` en el CRM pero
   localmente la llamada terminó hace rato → `CRM_STATUS_MISMATCH`

Un issue **no corrige** nada. Se abre para que una persona decida. Corregir
automáticamente el CRM desde acá es cómo se pierden datos sin que nadie lo
note.

parameters.query:
INSERT INTO wf_reconciliation_issues
  (issue_key, issue_type, entity_type, entity_id, lead_id, country_iso,
   severity, state, detail_json, first_seen_at, last_seen_at)
SELECT CONCAT('CRM_ACCOUNT_MISSING:lead:', e.lead_id), 'CRM_ACCOUNT_MISSING',
       'lead', e.lead_id, e.lead_id, e.country_iso, 'WARN', 'OPEN',
       JSON_OBJECT('local_event', e.event_key, 'provider', e.provider,
                   'crm_stage', c.stage, 'crm_account_opened', 0),
       UTC_TIMESTAMP(), UTC_TIMESTAMP()
  FROM wf_events e
  JOIN crm_leads c ON c.lead_id = e.lead_id
 WHERE e.event_type = 'ACCOUNT_CREATED'
   AND e.occurred_at >= DATE_SUB(UTC_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 7 DAY)
   AND COALESCE(c.stage, '') <> 'INTERESTED'
ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE occurrences = occurrences + 1,
        last_seen_at = UTC_TIMESTAMP(), detail_json = VALUES(detail_json)

INSERT INTO wf_reconciliation_issues
  (issue_key, issue_type, entity_type, entity_id, lead_id, country_iso,
   severity, state, detail_json, first_seen_at, last_seen_at)
SELECT CONCAT('CRM_STATUS_MISMATCH:lead:', c.lead_id), 'CRM_STATUS_MISMATCH',
       'lead', c.lead_id, c.lead_id, j.country_iso, 'WARN', 'OPEN',
       JSON_OBJECT('crm_status', c.status, 'local_state', j.state,
                   'local_result', j.result, 'call_job_id', j.call_job_id),
       UTC_TIMESTAMP(), UTC_TIMESTAMP()
  FROM crm_leads c
  JOIN wf_call_jobs j ON j.lead_id = c.lead_id
 WHERE c.status = 'ATTEMPTING' AND j.state = 'COMPLETED'
   AND j.completed_at < DATE_SUB(UTC_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 2 HOUR)
   AND j.completed_at >= DATE_SUB(UTC_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 2 DAY)
ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE occurrences = occurrences + 1,
        last_seen_at = UTC_TIMESTAMP(), detail_json = VALUES(detail_json)

parameters.content:
## 08 — PROVIDER RECONCILE

Se conserva el volcado del call-log
del worker Stringee a `stringee_calls` (volumen y duración reales del
proveedor), para poder contrastar lo que facturó el proveedor contra lo que
registró el suite.

`from_start_time` va en **segundos** (Stringee rechaza milisegundos). Ese
detalle costó una tarde en v1 y queda anotado acá.

parameters.query:
INSERT INTO stringee_calls
  (call_id, lead_id, phone, country, answered, duration_secs, start_time,
   answer_time, stop_time)
SELECT t.call_id,
       (SELECT c.lead_id FROM crm_leads c
         WHERE RIGHT(c.phone, 10) = RIGHT(t.phone, 10) LIMIT 1),
       t.phone,
       CASE WHEN t.phone LIKE '977%' THEN 'nepal'
            WHEN t.phone LIKE '52%'  THEN 'mexico'
            WHEN t.phone LIKE '91%'  THEN 'india'
            ELSE 'unknown' END,
       t.answered, t.duration_secs, t.start_time, t.answer_time, t.stop_time
  FROM JSON_TABLE(?, '$[*]' COLUMNS (
        call_id VARCHAR(64) PATH '$.call_id',
        phone VARCHAR(32) PATH '$.phone',
        answered INT PATH '$.answered',
        duration_secs INT PATH '$.duration_secs',
        start_time BIGINT PATH '$.start_time',
        answer_time BIGINT PATH '$.answer_time',
        stop_time BIGINT PATH '$.stop_time')) AS t
ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE
  lead_id = COALESCE(VALUES(lead_id), lead_id), country = VALUES(country),
  answered = VALUES(answered), duration_secs = VALUES(duration_secs),
  answer_time = VALUES(answer_time), stop_time = VALUES(stop_time)

parameters.content:
## 09 — SUMMARY

Resumen de la corrida y registro en
`panel_sync_log` (compatibilidad con las pantallas existentes).

Lo que **no** hay acá: ningún cálculo de KPI. Los números del panel salen de
`wf_call_jobs` y `wf_events`, en tiempo real, sin pasar por este workflow.

parameters.query:
SELECT
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM wf_call_jobs WHERE state = 'NEEDS_RECONCILIATION')
     AS jobs_needing_reconciliation,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM wf_call_jobs WHERE state = 'RELEASED') AS jobs_released,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM wf_conversation_ledger
    WHERE state = 'NEEDS_RECONCILIATION') AS ledger_needing_reconciliation,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM wf_tool_requests
    WHERE state = 'NEEDS_RECONCILIATION') AS tools_needing_reconciliation,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM wf_recording_ledger WHERE state = 'ORPHAN')
     AS recordings_orphan,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM wf_reconciliation_issues WHERE state = 'OPEN')
     AS issues_open

INSERT INTO panel_sync_log (source, rows_in, status, synced_at)
VALUES ('crm-v2', ?, 'ok', UTC_TIMESTAMP())
